title: Shaped by Default: From Narrative Capture to Deliberate Shaping
author: Mike Jones
summary: Most organizational strategies fail because they are disconnected from reality — functioning more like wish-fulfillment than genuine environmental engagement. When strategies do not produce results, leaders typically respond with control reflexes: centralizing decisions, increasing governance, and cutting functions — measures that gut the organizational intelligence needed to actually navigate complexity. Meanwhile, other actors in the environment are actively shaping conditions, building dependencies, and closing options. Organizations that lose contact with their operating environment become structurally coupled to dynamics they no longer see, arriving at decisions too late with diminished options. The antidote is organizational intelligence: treating strategy as a continuous practice of orientation — monitoring, experimenting, and interpreting the environment. Organizations that build intelligence and strategic position gain the ability to shape conditions rather than merely react to them, creating a compound advantage through five shaping modes: engage, frame, enable, constrain, and bind.
points: The 'control reflex' — centralizing decisions and cutting functions in response to execution failure — destroys the slack and intelligence that shaping requires, leaving organizations with only the ability to react.

Shaping is the deliberate alteration of an environment's rules, dependencies, expectations, and possibility-space so that future windows of opportunity open earlier and on better terms — five modes cover the full range: engage, frame, enable, constrain, and bind.
Framing — owning the narrative space before others act on it — is more durable than structural intervention because it changes what options appear as options at all for every other actor.

Binding (deliberately constraining your own options) can paradoxically increase your power over others, as it changes what other parties decide; this move is most often absent in organizations that keep options open as a matter of supposed prudence.

The difference between shaping and being shaped is not about capability or resources — it is whether the organization has maintained the capacity to act on its environment, or spent that capacity optimizing within conditions already configured by someone else.
quotes: This is the equivalent of making a wish in front of a birthday cake, changing nothing about how you live, and assuming the wish will find its way to you. Most strategy development takes this shape: declare a vision, let the machine run, produce the Greek Temple, amplify the narrative to the world, and try to optimise the parts while the whole fails to produce the effect required to shape the external environment to your advantage.

An organisation shaped by its own narrative has also lost the ability to see who is configuring the conditions it takes for granted. Leaders withdraw from or lose influence in the forums where direction is set, learning of decisions after they have happened.

The control reflex and better narratives only address symptoms. The only thing that addresses the root cause is rebuilding the capacity to see clearly, which means investing in organisational intelligence.

Framing is owning the narrative space; it is shaping how other actors understand the situation before acting on it. The organisation that shapes what the relevant actors treat as the obvious problem and the sensible response has done something more durable than any structural intervention.

Binding shapes others by constraining the organisation's own options, because doing so changes what the other parties decide. It rests on the paradox that the power to constrain another may depend on the power to bind oneself, and that the deliberate, irreversible surrender of a freedom can be a source of strength.

The external environment is not passive; it does not wait for you to be ready. Other actors are working on the conditions that will determine what is possible next. The organisation that has only been shaped will meet reality on terms it did not set and cannot easily change.
